newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls against basket as yen gains.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls against basket as yen gains.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed lower against the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday amid a sharp rise of the Japanese yen, dealers said.
"We saw high demand today for foreign currency, especially for the yen and Swiss franc. This demand for foreign currency pushed the basket upwards," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"Activity in the shekel-yen was high as investors continue to repay yen-linked loans following the recent rise of the yen against the dollar," he said.
Many Israeli companies turned to foreign currency loans during the last two years because of high domestic interest rates.
The U.S. currency fell on Tuesday to its lowest level against the yen since December 6.
The dealer added that the shekel remained stable against the dollar despite the decline of the U.S. currency abroad because of local demand for the dollar.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3910 shekels against 3.3920 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7007 shekels against 3.6927 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9896 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9161 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9968 shekels compared with 1.9922 on Monday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3950 shekels.
